name: Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses Ltd
title: Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses Ltd - 545000 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Zetwerk's record Q2 gross margin (~15%) and backlog of ₹14,500 cr (+67% YoY) signal demand outrunning capacity, with management admitting it is supply-constrained and relying on partners and captive capacity to deliver.

triggers.quote: Our order backlog in Q2 just 14,500 crores. It is the all-time high for the company. It is 67 percent higher compared to the same time last year.

triggers.label: Supply-constrained; capacity being added
triggers.quote: It fundamentally means we are a supply constraint company.

triggers.label: Manufacturing gross margin 25.5% record
triggers.quote: Gross profit and the percentage touched a historical high of 25.5 percent.

triggers.label: FY27 revenue growth 25–30%, adj. EBITDA ~70%
triggers.quote: our guidance on revenue is to grow the revenue by 25 to 30 percent for the full year.

Our guidance is we will grow this number by that same which is 70 percent range

red_flags.quote: we have taken some provisions in this business segment in the last year and quarter one of the current financial year.

summary.headline: Zetwerk Q2 FY27: adjusted EBITDA of Rs 171 crore, up 66% QoQ, with record order backlog of Rs 14,500 crore (up 67% YoY).
summary.overview: Management, speaking on the company's first results call after listing, reported Q2 FY27 revenue up 12% QoQ and gross profit up 39% QoQ, with gross margin near 15% versus 12% in the prior quarter. Adjusted EBITDA was Rs 171 crore, excluding non-cash ESOP expenses, and operating cash flow was still negative but improved about 67% QoQ and 50% YoY. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 25-30% and adjusted EBITDA growth of about 70%, with H2 expected to be larger than H1. Much of the Q&A focused on the business model, margin drivers, cash flow timing and exposure to US AI capex and India solar policy changes.

financial_highlights.value: Not stated as absolute figure; manufacturing segment Q2 revenue cited as up 30% QoQ

financial_highlights.change: vs 13% a year ago, 12% in Q1 FY27; gross profit +39% QoQ
vs 22% a year ago, 23% in prior quarter; described as all-time high
Ecosystem revenue +50% YoY in H1; -7% QoQ

financial_highlights.value: Rs 211 crore manufacturing; Rs 20 crore ecosystem

segments.name: Manufacturing business
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 9,400 crore at 19% gross margin; H1 FY27 revenue about Rs 4,400-4,500 crore at about 25% gross margin, with TTM gross margin near 21%. Energy is 64% of revenue, precision about 22%, and capital goods about 14%.

segments.name: Ecosystem business
segments.commentary: Pass-through supply of raw materials (aluminium, steel, zinc, copper) at 2-3% gross margin and about 1% EBITDA margin, with no inventory or commodity positions. H1 segment contribution about Rs 20 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 adjusted EBITDA guided to grow about 70% over FY26's Rs 420 crore.
H2 expected to be larger than H1 (historically H1 was about 40% of revenue and EBITDA in FY26); H2 mix expected to skew toward market-based model.
Full-year gross margin target: about 21% in FY27, rising 100-200 bps a year toward about 25%, possibly by FY29.
Operating cash flow expected to be around breakeven to positive for FY27 on a full-year basis; OCS was negative Rs 1-3 crore on TTM basis.
Discontinued operations: management expects no further provisions or losses; the business is near operational breakeven.
Post-IPO debt repayment expected to reduce finance cost materially in H2 FY27 and further in FY28. PAT expected to be positive in H2.
capex_capacity: Company is supply constrained: management says order backlog growth implies need to add capacity through both captive (in-house) factories and partner network.
Hybrid model: market-based (third-party SME suppliers, typically 45-50% utilisation) plus captive factories; 60% of H1 full payments were via captive and 40% via market-based.
Power transformer lead time offered at about 2 years versus 3-5 years industry norm; first transformer installed in US (North Carolina) in H1.
Revenue coverage of about 3 years (backlog plus new orders divided by current-year revenue); backlog conversion roughly two years.
Staffing: about 3,500 people, of which about 800 in design and engineering.
demand_pricing: Order backlog Rs 14,500 crore: 46% international, 33% ODM (own-design) business, 10-15% aerospace and defence; precision category orders up about 80% YoY.
Energy is 64% of revenue; India 59% and international 41% of revenue (international was 70% of revenue last year per management).
Repeat customers: 80-83% of revenue, range-bound for 3-4 years.
76% of revenue from build-to-print; 24% from own designs.
Gross margin by model: market-based 24% and captive 25% in H1 FY27; India 19% and international 32% in H1 FY27.
Pricing: premium taken on categories where lead time is much shorter (e.g. transformers at 2 years vs 3-4 years market).
US AI data-centre capex exposure estimated at 10-20% of order book; India solar orders of about Rs 500-2,000 crore won in H1 from domestic customers despite ALMM/DCR policy changes.

qa_highlights.question: Are clients paying a premium for Zetwerk products versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the captive model keeps margin headroom; in the market-based model SME suppliers run at 45-50% utilisation, so Zetwerk earns a take-rate. Premium pricing is taken where lead times are much shorter, e.g. transformers at 2 years versus 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: How hard is it to replicate electrification success in aerospace, defence and precision?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has Rs 1,500-2,000 crore of orders in the segment, has worked on it for 3-5 years, and uses founders to build categories before hiring professional CEOs (e.g. a senior transformer-business CEO hired from Hitachi). No formal category guidance was given; overall order book is expected to grow faster than the rest.

qa_highlights.question: When will operating cash flow turn positive and what is the working capital cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: TTM OCS was negative Rs 1-3 crore; management expects full-year FY27 OCS around breakeven to positive. Working capital cycle is about 30-31 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will PAT turn positive and what happens to finance cost and discontinued operations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects H2 PAT to be positive. Q2 finance cost was elevated by IPO-related items, which are one-time; post-IPO debt repayment should reduce finance cost. Discontinued operations are near breakeven, with no further provisions expected.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to US AI data-centre capex and India solar slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: US AI capex exposure is about 10-20% of order book, but management says customer RFQs and behaviour have not changed. In India solar, H1 won about Rs 500-2,000 crore from large domestic customers; the policy impact is seen as short-term.

qa_highlights.question: How will the supply chain be optimised across many product categories?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it matches material and process combinations (about 10-15 of ~100 permutations) and uses an in-house AI platform, ZEUS, to find suppliers and shorten RFQ response from 7-10 days toward 24 hours.

risks_watch: Supply constraint: backlog growth of 67% YoY may outpace capacity additions in captive and partner networks.
Operating cash flow still negative in Q2; management targets around breakeven to positive for full FY27, which needs to be tracked.
Ecosystem revenue is commodity-driven and fell 7% QoQ; the segment is low margin.
Exposure to US AI data-centre capex (about 10-20% of order book) and India solar policy changes (ALMM/DCR).
Q2 finance cost and discontinued-operation losses, which management says will decline in H2 but are not yet quantified.
Margin expansion depends on mix shift to aerospace/defence, international and captive work; H2 mix expected to skew toward market-based.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, backlog and margin trajectory; management repeatedly says margins will expand faster than revenue. More guarded on hard numbers and forward statements (e.g. declined to give formal category guidance and gave vague answers on OCS timing and Europe). Call audio was poor at points, so some answers were incomplete.
key_quotes: Our order backlog in Q2 just 14,500 crores. It is the all-time high for the company.
The gross margins are expanding to almost 15 percent compared to 13 percent same time last year and 12 percent in the prior quarter.
Gross margin is an input. Gross margin increase will happen through make 3M approach.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 25-30% and adjusted EBITDA growth of about 70% on a Rs 420 crore FY26 base, backed by a record Rs 14,500 crore order backlog (+67% YoY) and H1 orders of Rs 7,800 crore (+50% YoY), with the company self-described as supply constrained and adding captive and partner capacity, though no specific new plant commissioning timelines or capex figures were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Full-year FY27 gross margin guided near 21% (TTM ~21%, H1 manufacturing 25%), rising 100-200 bps a year toward ~25% by FY29, with H2 mix skewing to market-based and post-IPO debt repayment cutting finance cost.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management says it is supply constrained with backlog up 67% YoY to Rs 14,500 crore and is adding captive factories and partner capacity, but no plant commissioning dates or capex amounts were given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided up 25-30% on a Rs 9,400 crore manufacturing base, backed by H1 orders of Rs 7,800 crore (+50% YoY) and an order book that converts over about two years.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed, but the supply-constrained backlog growth of 67% YoY and the need to add captive and partner capacity make a capex announcement plausible without a stated plan or amount.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H2 is expected to be larger than H1 and the order book is up 67% YoY, but management guided 25-30% revenue growth, so an upgrade is conditional on execution.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: TTM operating cash flow was still negative (Rs 1-3 crore), management gave vague answers on OCS timing, and India solar policy and US AI capex (10-20% of order book) remain exposures.

rows.label: Aerospace, defence and precision orders
rows.why: Precision orders are up about 80% YoY and aerospace/defence is 10-15% of the Rs 14,500 crore backlog (about Rs 1,500-2,000 crore of segment orders), with management expecting the order book to grow faster than the rest.

rows.label: Operating cash flow turning breakeven to positive in FY27
rows.why: Management targets breakeven to positive full-year OCS, but TTM OCS was negative Rs 1-3 crore in Q2 and the timing answer was vague.

rows.label: Lower finance cost and positive PAT in H2 FY27
rows.why: Post-IPO debt repayment is expected to cut finance cost materially in H2 FY27 and further in FY28, with PAT guided positive in H2, though the amounts were not quantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on backlog, margin trajectory and H2 PAT, but guarded on OCS timing, formal category guidance and Europe; analysts pressed on cash flow, margin drivers and exposure to US AI capex and India solar policy.
